evidence_chain: Fact: Powell's May 4, 2026 FY2026 Q2 release states backlog at March 31, 2026 totaled $1.8B, up 33% year over year, and that new orders were $490M, up 97% year over year. Source: https://powellindustriesinc.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/powell-industries-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results

Fact: The same FY2026 Q2 release states Powell received, after quarter-end, a data-center order exceeding $400M related to behind-the-meter design of on-site generation assets, and described it as the largest order in Powell history. Source: https://powellindustriesinc.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/powell-industries-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results
Fact: Powell's FY2026 Q2 Form 10-Q is filed with the SEC for the quarter ended March 31, 2026. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/80420/000008042026000070/powl-20260331.htm

Fact: Powell's FY2026 Q1 Form 10-Q disclosed backlog of $1.6B at December 31, 2025 and stated approximately $933M was expected to be recognized as revenue within the next twelve months; backlog mix at that date included oil and gas, electric utility, and commercial/other industrial markets. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080420/000008042026000015/powl-20251231.htm

Fact: Powell's FY2026 Q1 result release said rapid data-center development and AI investment were creating larger and more numerous opportunities for Powell in Commercial & Other Industrial, specifically highlighting medium-voltage switchgear for larger data centers. Source: https://powellindustriesinc.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/powell-industries-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-2026-results

Inference: The combination of a large backlog, explicit data-center order language, and medium-voltage switchgear commentary supports treating POWL as a direct electrical infrastructure bottleneck candidate rather than a generic industrial cyclicals screen.

Hypothesis: The market may still under-map POWL to the AI/data-center power chain because its labels and customer history span oil & gas, petrochemical, utility, LNG, and general industrial electrical equipment.
falsification_plan: Track FY2026 Q3 and Q4 revenue conversion against the March 31, 2026 backlog; downgrade if backlog does not convert within management's expected project windows.
Compare gross margin and operating margin as large data-center and utility projects enter revenue; downgrade if margin falls materially without a temporary, well-explained cause.
Require disclosure or call commentary on whether the $400M+ data-center order is multi-phase, multi-customer, repeatable, and appropriately priced; downgrade if it is concentrated and non-repeatable.
Monitor bookings, book-to-bill, cancellations, scope reductions, and customer delays; downgrade if backlog rises but book-to-bill deteriorates or cancellations increase.
Check capacity, hiring, capex, supplier lead time, and labor availability commentary; downgrade if management signals delivery bottlenecks, penalties, or inability to staff projects.
Benchmark against larger OEMs and niche peers in switchgear/electrical distribution; downgrade if competitors show faster share capture or materially better margin resilience.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: The hidden supply-chain signal is whether the $1.8B backlog at March 31, 2026 and the post-quarter data-center order exceeding $400M represent durable bottleneck economics in custom medium-voltage electrical infrastructure, rather than a temporary lump from a few mega projects. Upgrade evidence would include rising data-center/utility mix, stable or expanding gross margin during project ramp, high book-to-bill, repeated data-center orders from multiple customers, and clear capacity/hiring plans without margin dilution. Falsifying evidence would include margin compression, order cancellations or scope reductions, delivery penalties, one-customer dependence, or backlog that fails to convert on the expected schedule.
next_research_tasks: Read the full FY2026 Q2 10-Q and extract backlog by market, expected revenue recognition timeline, contract asset/liability movement, customer concentration, warranty provisions, and risk-factor changes.

Review the FY2026 Q2 earnings call transcript for management commentary on the $400M+ data-center order, behind-the-meter scope, project duration, customer identity limits, pricing model, and margin expectations.

Build a backlog bridge: FY2025 ending backlog -> FY2026 Q1 backlog -> FY2026 Q2 backlog -> post-quarter $400M+ award, separating LNG, electric utility, commercial/other industrial, and data-center orders where possible.
Create a margin stress test for fixed-price contracts using scenarios for steel/copper/electrical component inflation, tariffs, overtime labor, delivery delays, and warranty/penalty exposure.
Map competitors and substitutes: Schneider Electric, Eaton, ABB, Siemens, GE Vernova, Vertiv-adjacent power systems, private switchgear/e-house specialists, and EPC procurement channels.

Verify product purity by segment: quantify how much revenue and backlog is tied to medium-voltage switchgear, integrated power control rooms, e-houses, substations, bus duct, field service, and power automation/control.

Check whether Powell is expanding facilities, adding shifts, hiring engineers/electricians, investing in testing capacity, or acquiring capabilities; these would be signals that demand is stressing internal capacity.
Monitor customer concentration disclosures in future 10-Q/10-K filings and compare revenue dependence on top customers before and after the data-center mega order begins conversion.
risks: Execution risk: custom-engineered, large electrical infrastructure orders can carry delivery, project-management, labor, engineering, and supplier coordination risk.
Margin risk: if large projects are fixed-price or poorly indexed to material, labor, tariff, or component inflation, backlog may convert at lower gross margin than expected.
Concentration risk: the post-quarter data-center order exceeding $400M may be customer- or project-concentrated; if it is a one-off mega award, the durability of the thesis weakens.
Backlog quality risk: backlog can be cancelled, modified, delayed, or repriced; backlog size alone is not proof of future revenue or profitability.
Capacity risk: demand may exceed Powell's ability to scale manufacturing, engineering, field service, testing, or skilled labor without bottlenecks or cost overruns.
Competition risk: larger electrical OEMs and integrated power-equipment suppliers may capture more of the same demand, limiting Powell's pricing power.
Cyclicality risk: Powell still has exposure to LNG, oil & gas, petrochemical, utility and industrial capex cycles, which can create lumpy bookings and revenue volatility.

Valuation/pricing risk: medium attention and recent order headlines may mean part of the backlog story is already reflected in market expectations; this report does not make a buy/sell recommendation.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand driver -> AI/data-center power load growth, utility grid expansion, LNG and industrial electrification. System node -> site electrical distribution, behind-the-meter power architecture, substation and power-control rooms. Product node -> custom-engineered medium-voltage switchgear, electrical distribution/control equipment, integrated power control rooms, e-houses, bus duct, substations, field service and related engineered solutions. Bottleneck hypothesis -> long-cycle custom electrical systems require engineering, manufacturing capacity, skilled labor, supplier components, customer qualification, project execution discipline, and delivery reliability; these constraints may be harder to scale than simple product volume.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：POWL 不是泛泛的数据中心受益标的，而是更直接地暴露在数据中心、工业项目、公用事业和 LNG 项目所需的中压开关柜、集成电力控制室、e-house、变电站、母线槽和电气配电控制系统。已核验证据显示，公司 FY2026 Q2 backlog 达到 18 亿美元，同比增长 33%；公司还披露季后获得一笔超过 4 亿美元的数据中心订单，为公司历史最大订单。Serenity 核心检验不是订单本身，而是这些订单能否在不牺牲毛利率、交付周期和客户/项目集中度风险的情况下转化为收入。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: POWL is not merely a generic data-center beneficiary; it has direct exposure to medium-voltage switchgear, integrated power control rooms, e-houses, substations, bus duct, and electrical power distribution/control systems required by data centers, utilities, LNG, and industrial electrification projects. Verified evidence shows FY2026 Q2 backlog of $1.8B, up 33% year over year, and a post-quarter data-center award exceeding $400M, described by the company as its largest order ever. The Serenity test is not the order headline itself, but whether the backlog converts into revenue while preserving gross margin, delivery reliability, and acceptable customer/project concentration.
deep_reports.title_cn: POWL：AI 数据中心电力链里的中压配电与预制电气系统卡点
deep_reports.title_en: POWL: Medium-Voltage Distribution and Prefabricated Electrical Systems Chokepoint in the AI/Data-Center Power Chain
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: POWL can be screened as a cyclical, niche industrial electrical manufacturer rather than as a pure-ish AI/data-center power infrastructure bottleneck. It sits one or two steps away from the obvious AI semiconductor and hyperscaler capex narratives, and its legacy exposure to oil & gas, petrochemical, LNG, utility and industrial markets can obscure the data-center power signal. This makes it less visible than mega-cap electrical OEMs, power semis, utilities, or data-center REITs, even though its backlog and order language now directly reference large data-center electrical infrastructure projects.

evidence_chain: [Fact] PLPC reported 2025 net sales of $669.3 million, up 13% from 2024; gross profit was $208.5 million; operating income was $55.1 million; net income attributable to shareholders was $35.3 million. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PLPC/10-k-preformed-line-products-co-files-annual-report-08025e7d7a3c.html

[Fact] Energy Products represented approximately 71% of revenue in both 2025 and 2024, up from 64% in 2023; Communications represented 22% in 2025, and Special Industries 7%. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PLPC/10-k-preformed-line-products-co-files-annual-report-08025e7d7a3c.html

[Fact] PLPC describes Energy Products as used for supporting, protecting, terminating, and splicing transmission and distribution lines, and as including bolted, welded, and compressed connectors for substations. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PLPC/10-k-preformed-line-products-co-files-annual-report-08025e7d7a3c.html

[Fact] PLPC offers products for OPGW and ADSS fiber optic cables, which the company says are commonly used to monitor and control power networks. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PLPC/10-k-preformed-line-products-co-files-annual-report-08025e7d7a3c.html

[Fact] Additional Energy Products include string hardware, polymer insulators, wildlife protection, substation fittings, and spacer dampers. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PLPC/10-k-preformed-line-products-co-files-annual-report-08025e7d7a3c.html

[Fact] PLPC states that the need for grid reliability, resilience, and aging-infrastructure upgrades is a market driver, and says it is positioned for growth as transmission grids, distribution lines, and substation projects are enhanced, upgraded, and extended. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PLPC/10-k-preformed-line-products-co-files-annual-report-08025e7d7a3c.html

[Fact] PLPC reported year-end 2025 backlog of approximately $232.8 million, up about 22% from the prior year, and said substantially all of that backlog was expected to ship in 2026. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/PLPC/10-k-preformed-line-products-co-files-annual-report-08025e7d7a3c.html

[Fact] On May 5, 2026, PLPC announced the acquisition of Delta Star Conetores Elétricos Ltda., a Brazil-based manufacturer specializing in HV and EHV substation connectors. Source: https://plp.com/news-events/254-plp-expands-global-substation-portfolio-with-acquisition-of-delta-star-conetores-eletricos-ltda

[Fact] PLPC said the Delta Star acquisition expands its global substation hardware and components portfolio and complements prior acquisitions of SubCon Electrical Fittings in Austria, Maxxweld Conectores in Brazil, and Delta Conectores in Mexico. Source: https://plp.com/news-events/254-plp-expands-global-substation-portfolio-with-acquisition-of-delta-star-conetores-eletricos-ltda
[Fact] PLPC's market cap was approximately $1.84 billion as of June 8, 2026, based on the finance tool quote. Source: finance tool result for PLPC, June 8, 2026.

[Inference] The Energy Products mix and Delta Star acquisition direction strengthen the grid-hardware exposure case, but current public evidence does not yet prove a direct data-center interconnection revenue link.

[Inference] Backlog growth supports demand strength, but because backlog is not disclosed by Energy Products, substation hardware, HV/EHV connectors, or data-center-related projects, it cannot yet be treated as proof of a substation chokepoint.

[Hypothesis] If PLPC's connectors, formed wire, OPGW/ADSS, and substation fittings are qualification-sensitive and difficult to substitute in utility/EPC project schedules, PLPC could have more bottleneck value than the market assigns to a mixed infrastructure supplier.

[Speculation] The Delta Star acquisition could be an early sign that PLPC is intentionally consolidating niche substation connector capacity globally; this needs confirmation through purchase price, revenue contribution, margins, customer overlap, and order conversion.
falsification_plan: Falsify if Energy Products revenue share falls materially, or Energy Products growth slows while communications or unrelated products drive most company growth.
Falsify if future filings show Delta Star revenue, backlog, or profit contribution is immaterial relative to PLPC's consolidated revenue and Energy Products base.
Falsify if management does not disclose any incremental substation, transmission, HV/EHV, or utility customer momentum after the Delta Star acquisition.
Falsify if gross margin continues to compress despite rising energy/grid sales, indicating weak pricing power and limited bottleneck control.
Falsify if backlog growth reverses or remains broad-based without evidence of energy, transmission, distribution, or substation project concentration.
Falsify if PLPC's acquired substation connector assets mainly serve regional or low-voltage demand rather than HV/EHV grid modernization needs.
Falsify if utilities/EPCs treat PLPC products as easily substitutable commodity hardware with no qualification, reliability, or delivery-time advantage.

Falsify the data-center interconnection angle unless customer disclosures, project references, EPC relationships, or utility-capex commentary tie PLPC products to substation upgrades serving large-load interconnections.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Energy Products, substation hardware, and the Delta Star Conetores Elétricos acquisition materially increase PLPC's exposure to high-voltage and extra-high-voltage substation demand, rather than leaving the company as a diversified energy/communications infrastructure supplier with only moderate grid leverage.
next_research_tasks: Pull PLPC's latest 10-Q after the May 2026 Delta Star close and check whether acquisition accounting, purchase price allocation, revenue contribution, backlog, intangibles, customer relationships, or integration costs are disclosed.

Build a product-by-product grid exposure map: formed wire, substation connectors, OPGW/ADSS, ADSS hardware, spacer dampers, string hardware, polymer insulators, wildlife protection, substation fittings, inspection services.
Check whether PLPC investor presentations disclose Energy Products revenue by transmission, distribution, substation, renewables, communications-on-utility, or inspection categories.
Search utility and EPC procurement records for PLPC, Delta Star, SubCon Electrical Fittings, Maxxweld Conectores, and Delta Conectores references in transmission/substation projects.
Compare PLPC's gross margin and operating margin trends against reference grid-equipment suppliers and niche hardware peers to distinguish volume growth from bottleneck pricing.
Verify whether OPGW/ADSS demand is tied to grid monitoring/control, utility fiber, and grid modernization programs rather than general broadband only.
Investigate customer concentration: identify the customer representing 10.7% of 2025 consolidated revenue if possible, and determine whether it is a utility, distributor, telecom operator, or EPC.
Track hiring, capex, plant expansions, and engineering/sales headcount specifically tied to Energy Products, substation products, and recent acquisitions.
Review patents, certifications, ISO/utility approvals, and field reliability standards to assess whether PLPC products have long qualification cycles or easy substitutes.
Monitor Q2/Q3 2026 commentary for any references to HV/EHV substations, U.S. substation business, grid reliability/resilience, transmission upgrades, and Delta Star order flow.
risks: [Evidence risk] PLPC does not yet provide enough public granularity to isolate HV/EHV substation connector revenue, Delta Star contribution, or data-center interconnection exposure.
[Business-mix risk] Communications and Special Industries remain meaningful, so the company is not a pure grid-capex vehicle.

[Commodity/input risk] PLPC cited tariffs, steel, aluminum, manufacturing costs, transportation costs, and inflation as operating pressures; 2025 gross margin declined from 32.0% to 31.2% despite revenue growth.
[Pricing-power risk] Higher sales volumes may not translate into higher margins if products are more commodity-like than bottleneck-like.

[Acquisition/integration risk] Delta Star may be strategically relevant but financially immaterial, dilutive, or slow to integrate; the deal was announced after Q1 2026, so contribution evidence is not yet visible in reported results.
[Customer/project timing risk] Utility and EPC demand can be lumpy, budget-driven, and delayed by permitting, rate cases, transmission planning, and interconnection queues.
[Substitution risk] If utilities can source similar connectors and line hardware from broad industrial suppliers without long qualification cycles, the chokepoint thesis weakens.

[Valuation/attention risk] The stock had a market cap around $1.84 billion on June 8, 2026, and strong price appreciation could mean part of the hidden grid thesis is already being recognized, even if media attention remains low.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand driver: electrification, grid reliability/resilience spending, transmission expansion, distribution upgrades, substation projects, broadband/fiber buildouts on utility networks, and potential data-center interconnection needs. System layer: electric utilities, EPCs, substation OEMs, line contractors, broadband/utility communications operators. PLPC node: formed wire products; transmission and distribution line hardware; support/protection/termination/splicing products; bolted, welded, and compressed substation connectors; OPGW and ADSS hardware used for grid monitoring/control; string hardware; polymer insulators; wildlife protection; substation fittings; spacer dampers; utility inspection services. Bottleneck hypothesis: not a single proprietary mega-component, but a basket of qualified, project-critical, field-reliable hardware that must be available on schedule for line and substation construction. Public-market mapping: underfollowed small-cap supplier rather than reference-leader transformer/switchgear names.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: PLPC 可能是电网扩建、输配电升级、变电站改造和电力通信融合的二阶受益者。它不是显性的变压器、开关柜或数据中心电力设备公司，而是处在支持、保护、终端、接续输配电线路，以及变电站连接件、OPGW/ADSS、线路硬件、绝缘、防护和检测服务等更细碎但必要的节点。公司 2025 年 Energy Products 占收入约 71%，且 Energy Products 包括输配电线路支撑/保护/终端/接续产品、变电站连接件、OPGW/ADSS、string hardware、polymer insulators、wildlife protection、substation fittings 和 spacer dampers。如果电网建设瓶颈不仅在大型主设备，也在项目交付所需的连接、支撑、保护和线路硬件，那么 PLPC 可能受益于市场从“显性电力设备”向“施工与并网必需件”的再定价。但目前升级为强 thesis 的关键证据仍缺失：Delta Star 收入/订单/利润贡献、HV/EHV substation backlog、客户认证与交付周期、以及能源产品毛利是否体现瓶颈定价权。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Hypothesis] PLPC may be a second-order beneficiary of grid expansion, T&D upgrades, substation modernization, and the convergence of electric power and grid communications. It is not an obvious transformer, switchgear, or data-center power-equipment story; it sits in smaller but necessary nodes such as T&D line support/protection/termination/splicing hardware, substation connectors, OPGW/ADSS, line hardware, insulation, wildlife protection, motion-control devices, and utility inspection services. [Fact] Energy Products represented about 71% of 2025 revenue, and PLPC discloses that Energy Products include T&D line support/protection/termination/splicing products, substation connectors, OPGW/ADSS, string hardware, polymer insulators, wildlife protection, substation fittings, and spacer dampers. [Inference] If grid bottlenecks extend beyond large electrical equipment into the connectors, protection, support, and line-hardware needed to physically deliver projects, PLPC could benefit from a market rotation from obvious power-equipment names toward hidden buildout enablers. However, the thesis still needs stronger proof: Delta Star revenue/order/profit contribution, HV/EHV substation backlog, customer qualification evidence, delivery-cycle constraints, and segment-level margin evidence that grid hardware has bottleneck-like pricing power.
deep_reports.title_cn: PLPC：隐藏在输配电线路、OPGW/ADSS 与变电站连接件里的电网硬件候选
deep_reports.title_en: PLPC: A hidden grid-hardware candidate inside T&D line hardware, OPGW/ADSS, and substation connectors
deep_reports.why_underfollowed: PLPC may be missed because it is classified and perceived as a mixed energy/communications/broadband/inspection infrastructure company rather than a pure AI-power or grid-capex company. Its products are not headline components like transformers, switchgear, turbines, generators, or data-center cooling. The signal is buried in product categories such as formed wire, connectors, OPGW/ADSS, utility pole line hardware, substation fittings, and inspection services. Its acquisition strategy also looks incremental and geographically fragmented, even though the May 2026 Delta Star deal explicitly targets HV/EHV substation connectors.

evidence_chain: MYR reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1.00 billion, up $166.8 million year over year; T&D revenue was $541.0 million and C&I revenue was $459.4 million. Source: MYR Group Q1 2026 results, https://investor.myrgroup.com/node/16251

As of March 31, 2026, MYR backlog was $2.84 billion, up 7.7% year over year; T&D backlog was $980.7 million and C&I backlog was $1.86 billion. Source: MYR Group Q1 2026 results, https://investor.myrgroup.com/node/16251

MYR’s Q1 2026 investor presentation describes the company as a market leader in electrical construction, with 9,000+ employees, 65+ office locations, 90%+ repeat clients, and services spanning Transmission, Distribution, Substation, Energy Storage, Manufacturing, Data Centers, Clean Energy, and related markets. Source: SEC-filed investor presentation, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/700923/000070092326000030/myrginvestorpresentation.htm

The same investor presentation states that data centers have been an important and growing C&I end market and that new interconnections, substations, and infrastructure upgrades to data centers create opportunities for the T&D segment. Source: SEC-filed investor presentation, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/700923/000070092326000030/myrginvestorpresentation.htm

On the Q1 2026 earnings call, management cited awards including an Arizona MSA spanning transmission, distribution and substations; two greenfield substations in Texas; substation work in Arizona; a 345 kV transmission-line project in South Carolina; and other overhead transmission and distribution work. Source: Q1 2026 corrected transcript, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/e6ebdf11-b6d6-4f30-b0f0-ba45726ea9ab

On the Q1 2026 earnings call, C&I management said data-center projects and water/wastewater projects are driving the strongest growth in the construction market, and disclosed multiple data-center project awards in New Jersey, Arizona, California, and Colorado. Source: Q1 2026 corrected transcript, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/e6ebdf11-b6d6-4f30-b0f0-ba45726ea9ab

MYR’s 2025 Form 10-K shows 2025 contract revenues of $2.00 billion in T&D and $1.66 billion in C&I, with operating income margins of 7.9% and 5.9%, respectively. Source: 2025 Form 10-K, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/f15fbf6f-78c7-4fbc-801a-5638665c2d1c

MYR’s 2025 Form 10-K also highlights execution risk: 2025 T&D margins were negatively affected by labor and project inefficiencies on certain projects, and C&I margins were negatively affected by labor/project inefficiencies and unfavorable change orders. Source: 2025 Form 10-K, https://investor.myrgroup.com/static-files/f15fbf6f-78c7-4fbc-801a-5638665c2d1c
As of June 8, 2026 around 18:30 UTC, MYRG market capitalization was approximately $6.96 billion. Source: market data retrieved via finance tool.

The evidence supports that MYRG has real exposure to data centers, substations, T&D, and interconnect-style infrastructure; however, the company has not yet provided enough granular backlog disclosure to prove that AI/data-center power infrastructure is the dominant driver.

If the electrical-construction labor and commissioning pool becomes a binding constraint for data-center and grid projects, MYRG’s execution capacity could command better backlog quality, better project selectivity, and possibly more resilient demand than generic construction peers.
falsification_plan: Falsify if future backlog growth is mostly generic commercial construction, transportation, or non-power C&I work rather than data centers, substations, T&D, utility interconnects, grid modernization, or high-voltage projects.
Falsify if backlog rises but gross margin and operating margin deteriorate because of fixed-price contracts, labor inefficiencies, unfavorable change orders, or poor project closeout.
Falsify if management stops citing data-center, substation, interconnection, or T&D awards while AI data-center and utility capex remain strong elsewhere.
Falsify if labor constraints prevent MYRG from converting backlog to revenue, causing delays, claims, or working-capital strain.
Falsify if large utilities, data-center developers, or hyperscalers appear to consolidate work away from MYRG subsidiaries toward larger EPC competitors.
Falsify if book-to-bill and backlog decline in T&D and C&I while broader grid and data-center power indicators remain strong, suggesting MYRG lacks competitive capture.
Falsify if cash conversion deteriorates materially through claims, contract assets, receivables, or disputed change orders, indicating that reported backlog quality is weaker than headline figures.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog growth, book-to-bill, margin improvement, and project awards are specifically tied to grid modernization, substations, utility interconnects, high-voltage transmission, and data-center electrical infrastructure rather than broad nonresidential construction.
next_research_tasks: Extract three-year backlog by segment from 10-Ks and 10-Qs: total backlog, T&D backlog, C&I backlog, book-to-bill, and backlog-to-forward-revenue conversion.

Build a keyword table from 2024-2026 filings and transcripts: data center, hyperscale, AI, substation, interconnect, transmission, distribution, grid modernization, MSA, fixed price, change order, labor, productivity, safety, commissioning.

Compare MYRG to reference leaders and peers in two lanes: obvious power-equipment names versus execution-layer contractors such as Quanta Services, MasTec, EMCOR, IES Holdings, and other electrical contractors. The goal is not to recommend a stock but to test relative purity of exposure and evidence quality.
Review contract mix disclosures: fixed-price, unit-price, T&E, cost-plus, reimbursable, MSAs, and whether higher data-center exposure increases or decreases risk.
Check working-capital quality each quarter: contract assets, contract liabilities, receivable days, claims, change orders, cash conversion, and free cash flow versus EBITDA.
Track labor signals: headcount, wage inflation, union/non-union mix where disclosed, subcontractor dependence, OSHA/safety metrics, TCIR, LTIR, and recruiting/training commentary.
Map announced project geographies to data-center and grid-load hotspots: Arizona, Texas, Colorado, California, New Jersey, South Carolina, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Iowa, and Canada.

Search utility commission filings, interconnection queues, local permits, and data-center development records for MYRG subsidiary names to confirm whether disclosed awards connect to large-load power infrastructure.

Monitor whether management gives more granular end-market disclosure in future investor presentations, especially percentage of C&I backlog tied to data centers and percentage of T&D backlog tied to substations/interconnections.

Create a falsification dashboard item that flags any quarter with backlog growth but margin compression, negative estimate changes, rising contract assets, or language about unfavorable change orders.
risks: Electrical construction is project-execution intensive. Labor inefficiencies, productivity misses, safety incidents, unfavorable change orders, project delays, and closeout disputes can erase the apparent benefit of strong demand.
C&I revenue growth in Q1 2026 was primarily tied to fixed-price contracts, and fixed-price exposure can pressure margins if labor, materials, subcontractor, or schedule assumptions are wrong.
Reported backlog may not map cleanly to AI/data-center power infrastructure. If backlog is dominated by lower-margin or generic construction work, the chokepoint thesis weakens.

C&I demand still includes broader commercial, transportation, manufacturing, water/wastewater, clean-energy, and other markets. A slowdown in nonresidential construction could offset strength in data centers.
The same skilled-labor scarcity that creates a potential moat can also limit revenue conversion or raise wage costs.
Large utilities, hyperscalers, or data-center developers may route work through larger EPCs, preferred vendors, or bundled equipment-and-services providers.

The 2025 Form 10-K shows both T&D and C&I margins were affected by estimate changes, labor/project inefficiencies, and change-order dynamics, confirming that the business can be volatile even in favorable demand environments.

Although the candidate is underfollowed by theme investors, the stock is no longer extremely cheap or obscure by size, with market cap around $7 billion on June 8, 2026. Any report should avoid treating underfollowed thematic exposure as a valuation conclusion.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Demand driver: AI data centers, electrification, reshoring, grid modernization, renewable interconnection, power reliability. System bottleneck: power availability and grid connection. Physical asset layer: transmission lines, distribution systems, substations, interconnects, data-center electrical rooms, energy storage, clean-energy tie-ins. Execution layer: electrical EPC, specialty electrical construction, project management, procurement coordination, skilled labor, testing, commissioning, safety and quality control. MYRG sits primarily in the execution layer across T&D and C&I, with exposure to substations, transmission, distribution, data centers, manufacturing, transportation, clean energy, and energy storage.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: MYRG 可能是 AI 数据中心与电网升级链条中的二阶卡点。市场通常先关注变压器、开关柜、电缆、燃机、核电或公用事业资产，但即便设备可得，项目仍需要合格电气施工队伍、变电站施工、T&D 升级、并网执行、采购协调、测试和调试能力才能真正落地。MYRG 的公开材料显示其业务覆盖 Transmission & Distribution、substation、data centers、clean energy、energy storage、manufacturing 等场景，并在 2026 年一季度披露了数据中心项目、变电站项目、345 kV transmission line 项目以及 record backlog。该 thesis 的关键升级点是：如果后续披露显示 backlog 与收入增长主要来自数据中心电力接入、变电站、T&D、grid modernization、utility interconnect 和高复杂度电气基础设施，而不是普通商业建筑周期，则 MYRG 的供应链位置应从“普通 specialty contractor”上调为“电力基础设施执行能力瓶颈”。
deep_reports.thesis_en: MYRG may be a second-order chokepoint in AI data-center power deployment and grid modernization. The market often focuses first on transformers, switchgear, cables, turbines, nuclear, or regulated utilities, but even when hardware is available, projects still require qualified electrical construction labor, substation construction, T&D upgrades, interconnection execution, procurement coordination, testing, and commissioning. Recent MYRG disclosures connect the company to Transmission & Distribution, substations, data centers, clean energy, energy storage, manufacturing, and large electrical construction. Q1 2026 materials also cite data-center awards, substation awards, a 345 kV transmission-line project, and record backlog. The key upgrade condition is evidence that backlog and revenue growth are specifically tied to data-center power connections, substations, T&D, grid modernization, utility interconnects, and high-complexity electrical infrastructure rather than generic commercial construction.

That label can cause investors screening for energy bottlenecks to focus on more obvious hardware suppliers or regulated utilities while missing the execution constraint.
